name: history
description: Use when you need to know whether a fault is new, recurring or came back after a clear, or how a value compares with this car's past drives.
instructions: The triage step already ran read_history {"limit":5}: read its section first. Call read_history {"limit":10} only when you need older AI runs or checks.
Call history_compare with one Mode 01 PID, e.g. {"pid":"0105"}, to put a reading now next to its max and average on this car's last 10 trips (oldest first).
History is what this phone saved for this car only (AI runs, fault-code checks from the Fault codes screen, module scans); it says nothing about work done elsewhere.
interpret: "Recurring: P0401 (3 checks)" means the code was read in 3 of the listed checks: a lasting fault, not a one-off. A code seen once and then gone was probably intermittent or already fixed.

"Codes went away between A and B (cleared or fixed)": someone cleared the codes or the fault healed. A code that is back in a later check after that came back by itself: the repair, if any, did not hold.
A pending code that turns into a stored code over later checks is a fault getting confirmed.

In history_compare, a value now well outside the trips' max / average range (e.g. coolant max 90 °C on every trip, 105 °C now) points to a recent change; compare like with like (idle now vs. a drive's max).
"not logged" means that trip did not record the PID; it is not a zero reading.
